learn.hook: A photo and its enlarged poster look exactly alike, only bigger — that is similarity!
points: Congruent figures have the same shape and the same size. Similar figures have the same shape but not necessarily the same size.
Two polygons with the same number of sides are similar if their corresponding angles are equal AND their corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
All circles are similar, all squares are similar and all equilateral triangles are similar.
Every pair of congruent figures is similar, but similar figures need not be congruent.
In ΔABC ~ ΔPQR the order matters: A ↔ P, B ↔ Q, C ↔ R, so AB/PQ = BC/QR = CA/RP.

example.q: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR with AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm and PQ = 9 cm. Find QR.
steps: Corresponding sides are in the same ratio: AB/PQ = BC/QR

learn.reallife: Maps, building models and the zoom on your phone camera all make figures similar to the real thing.

games.title: Always similar?
items: Two circles
Two squares
Two equilateral triangles
Two rectangles
Two isosceles triangles
Two rhombuses
Two right triangles
Two regular hexagons

games.title: Same shape check
items: All circles are similar.
Any circle is just a scaled copy of another.
All rectangles are similar.
A 1 × 2 rectangle and a 1 × 5 rectangle have different shapes.
Two congruent figures are always similar.
They have the same shape (scale factor 1).
Two similar figures are always congruent.
Similar figures can be of different sizes.
All rhombuses are similar.
Their angles can be different, for example a square and a thin diamond.
For two polygons to be similar, equal angles alone are always enough.
A square and a long rectangle have equal angles but are not similar. Sides must be proportional too (triangles are a special case).

quiz.q: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF with AB = 4 cm, DE = 6 cm and BC = 5 cm. What is EF?
quiz.explain: AB/DE = BC/EF, so 4/6 = 5/EF and EF = 5 × 6 ÷ 4 = 7.5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds the difference 2 cm instead of using the ratio

quiz.q: Which pair of figures is ALWAYS similar?
quiz.explain: All squares have 90° angles and four equal sides, so one is always a scaled copy of the other.
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal angles alone make any polygons similar

quiz.q: A 10 cm × 15 cm photo is enlarged so that the 10 cm side becomes 25 cm. What does the 15 cm side become?
quiz.explain: The scale factor is 25/10 = 2.5, so the other side becomes 15 × 2.5 = 37.5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds 15 cm to the side instead of multiplying by the scale factor

quiz.q: ΔPQR ~ ΔXYZ, with ∠P = 50° and ∠Q = 70°. What is ∠Z?
quiz.explain: ∠Z corresponds to ∠R, and ∠R = 180° − 50° − 70° = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Matches the angles in the wrong order

quiz.q: Which conditions make two polygons with the same number of sides similar?
options: Corresponding angles equal and corresponding sides in the same ratio
quiz.explain: Both conditions are needed for polygons in general: equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one condition is always enough for any polygon

quiz.q: The scale factor from ΔABC to ΔPQR is 3. The perimeter of ΔABC is 12 cm. What is the perimeter of ΔPQR?
quiz.explain: Every side is multiplied by 3, so the perimeter is multiplied by 3: 12 × 3 = 36 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 to the perimeter or divides by 3

quiz.q: If ΔABC ~ ΔQRP, which angle is equal to ∠B?
quiz.explain: Read the letters in order: A ↔ Q, B ↔ R, C ↔ P. So ∠B = ∠R.
quiz.mistake: Matches letters by position in the alphabet instead of by order in the statement

quiz.q: On a map, 1 cm stands for 5 km. A road is 3.6 cm long on the map. How long is the real road?
quiz.explain: The map is similar to the real place with scale 1 : 5 km, so 3.6 × 5 = 18 km.
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 instead of multiplying by the scale

teach.ask: Gappu holds a small and a big photo of himself: 'Are these two pictures similar or congruent?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Same shape, maybe different size, with equal angles and sides in the same ratio. Similar!
teach.nudge: What must be the same, and what can be different, for two figures to be similar?

topics.title: Similarity in action: why both conditions matter

learn.hook: A square and a rhombus both have four equal sides — so why aren't they similar? Let's find out, and measure some triangles too!
points: Similarity lets us measure things we cannot reach — heights of towers and widths of rivers — using small, similar triangles.
For polygons, BOTH conditions are needed: equal corresponding angles AND proportional sides.

A square and a rhombus have proportional sides (all equal) but different angles, so they are not similar. A square and a rectangle have equal angles but sides not in the same ratio, so they are not similar either.
Activity: draw a triangle, draw lines parallel to one side, and measure. The two sides are always cut in the same ratio — this is what the Basic Proportionality Theorem proves.

example.q: A square has side 4 cm. A rectangle is 4 cm by 6 cm. Are they similar?
steps: Angles: both have four 90° angles, so the angles match
The side ratios are not all equal
So they are not similar, even though the angles are equal
example.answer: No — the angles match but the sides are not proportional

learn.reallife: Surveyors find the width of a river like the Ganga by drawing a small similar triangle on the bank — no boat needed!

games.title: Always similar or not always?
items: Two circles
Two squares
Two equilateral triangles
Two rectangles
Two rhombuses
Two isosceles triangles
Two right triangles
Two congruent triangles

games.title: Both conditions?
items: A square and a rhombus of the same side are similar.
Their sides match but their angles do not (unless the rhombus is a square).
A square and a rectangle are always similar because all angles are 90°.
The sides of a non-square rectangle are not in the same ratio as a square's.
Two triangles with equal corresponding angles are similar.
For triangles, equal angles are enough.
A parallel line in a triangle always cuts the other two sides in the same ratio.
Your measurements in the activity show it, and BPT proves it.
Similarity can help find the height of a tower without climbing it.
Compare its shadow with the shadow of a stick of known height.

quiz.q: A square and a rhombus both have side 5 cm, and the rhombus has angles 60° and 120°. Why are they not similar?
options: A rhombus has no equal sides
Their corresponding angles are not equal
They have different numbers of sides
quiz.explain: The side ratio is 5/5 = 1 for every pair, but the square's angles are 90° while the rhombus has 60° and 120°. Equal angles are also needed.
quiz.mistake: Thinks proportional sides alone are enough for polygons

quiz.q: A square is 3 cm by 3 cm and a rectangle is 3 cm by 5 cm. Which statement is true?
options: They are not similar because the sides are not in the same ratio
They are similar because all angles are 90°
They are similar because one side is equal
quiz.explain: Angles match, but 3/3 = 1 while 3/5 ≠ 1, so the sides are not proportional.
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal angles alone are enough for quadrilaterals

quiz.q: Which pair of figures is NOT always similar?
quiz.explain: Two rectangles can have different length-to-breadth ratios (like 2 × 3 and 2 × 5), so they need not be similar.
quiz.mistake: Assumes all figures of the same name are similar

quiz.q: How can similar triangles help you find the height of a tall tree without climbing it?
options: Count the leaves on the tree
It cannot be done without climbing
Measure the tree's shadow and the shadow of a stick of known height at the same time, then use equal ratios
quiz.explain: The tree and its shadow, and the stick and its shadow, form similar triangles. So height/shadow is the same for both.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect similarity with indirect measurement

quiz.q: In an activity, Asha draws DE ∥ BC in ΔABC and measures AD = 2.4 cm, DB = 3.6 cm, AE = 2 cm and EC = 3 cm. What does she notice?
quiz.explain: 2.4/3.6 = 2/3 and 2/3 = 2/3. The parallel line cuts both sides in the same ratio.
quiz.mistake: Compares lengths instead of ratios

quiz.q: In another triangle ABC, Asha draws PQ ∥ BC with P on AB and Q on AC. AP = 3 cm, PB = 3 cm and AQ = 2.5 cm. What should QC measure?
quiz.explain: AP/PB = 1, so AQ/QC must also be 1: QC = 2.5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Copies PB instead of using the ratio

quiz.q: Which pair are similar figures?
options: A square tile and a rectangular tile
An equilateral triangle and a right triangle
A photo and its enlarged print with the same shape
A rhombus with a 60° angle and a square
quiz.explain: An enlargement keeps all angles and multiplies every length by the same factor, so it is similar to the original.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any two figures with four sides are similar

quiz.q: Two congruent triangles are also similar. What is their scale factor?
quiz.explain: Congruent figures have equal sides, so each ratio is 1.
steps: Each side ratio = same length ÷ same length = 1
quiz.mistake: Thinks congruent figures cannot be similar

teach.ask: Gappu thinks a square and a rhombus with equal sides must be similar. Explain why not, and what two things similarity needs.
teach.praise: Chirp! Similar needs equal angles AND proportional sides — the rhombus fails on angles!
teach.nudge: Which condition does the rhombus fail?

learn.hook: Draw a line parallel to one side of a triangle and it slices the other two sides in exactly the same ratio!
points: Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales theorem): if a line parallel to one side of a triangle meets the other two sides at distinct points, it divides those sides in the same ratio.
In ΔABC with D on AB, E on AC and DE ∥ BC: AD/DB = AE/EC.
It also follows that AD/AB = AE/AC.
Converse: if a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.
Special case: the line through the midpoint of one side, parallel to another side, passes through the midpoint of the third side.

example.q: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 3 cm, DB = 4 cm and AE = 4.5 cm. Find EC.

learn.reallife: Carpenters making an A-frame stand fix crossbars parallel to the base; BPT tells them exactly where each bar must meet the two slanting legs.

items.text: If DE ∥ BC in ΔABC, then AD/DB = AE/___
DE ∥ BC with AD = 2, DB = 3 and AE = 4, so EC = ___
DE ∥ BC with AD = 5, AB = 15 and AE = 4, so AC = ___
If AD/DB = AE/EC, then DE is ___ to BC
A line through the midpoint of one side, parallel to a second side, meets the third side at its ___

quiz.q: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = 6 cm, DB = 9 cm and AE = 8 cm. What is EC?
quiz.explain: AD/DB = AE/EC gives 6/9 = 8/EC, so EC = 8 × 9 ÷ 6 = 12 cm.
quiz.mistake: Flips the ratio and gets 8 × 6 ÷ 9 ≈ 5.33

quiz.q: In ΔABC, D is on AB and E is on AC with AD = 3, DB = 5, AE = 4.5 and EC = 7.5. Is DE ∥ BC?
options: No, because the sides are not equal
Yes, by the converse of BPT
quiz.explain: AD/DB = 3/5 = 0.6 and AE/EC = 4.5/7.5 = 0.6. The ratios are equal, so DE ∥ BC by the converse of BPT.
quiz.mistake: Expects the pieces to be equal rather than in the same ratio

quiz.q: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC and AD/DB = 2/3. If AC = 20 cm, what is AE?
quiz.explain: AE/EC = 2/3, so AE is 2 parts out of 5 parts of AC: AE = 2/5 × 20 = 8 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses 2/3 of AC instead of 2/5

quiz.q: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = x, DB = x − 3, AE = x + 3 and EC = x − 2. Find x.
quiz.mistake: Makes a sign error when expanding (x + 3)(x − 3)

quiz.q: In ΔPQR, ST ∥ QR with S on PQ and T on PR. If PS/SQ = 3/4, what is PT/PR?
quiz.explain: PT/TR = 3/4, so PT is 3 parts of the 7 parts of PR: PT/PR = 3/7.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the part-to-part ratio with the part-to-whole ratio

quiz.q: D and E are the midpoints of AB and AC in ΔABC, and BC = 14 cm. What is DE?
quiz.explain: The segment joining the midpoints of two sides is parallel to the third side and half of it: 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks DE equals BC because they are parallel

quiz.q: By what other name is the Basic Proportionality Theorem known?
quiz.explain: It is named after the Greek mathematician Thales.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of famous theorems

quiz.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC, and its diagonals meet at O. Which ratio equals AO/OC?
quiz.explain: Draw a line through O parallel to AB and DC and apply BPT in two triangles. This shows the diagonals cut each other in the same ratio: AO/OC = BO/OD.
quiz.mistake: Writes the second ratio upside down

teach.ask: Gappu draws a line across a triangle: 'When does this line cut the sides in the same ratio?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Parallel to one side means the other two sides are cut in the same ratio. Thales says hi!
teach.nudge: What must be true about the line, and what happens to the two sides it cuts?

learn.hook: You don't need to check all six parts — just the right three clues prove two triangles are similar!
points: AAA (or AA) criterion: if two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the triangles are similar (the third angles are then equal too).
SSS criterion: if all three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, the triangles are similar.
SAS criterion: if one angle is equal and the sides including that angle are in the same ratio, the triangles are similar.
For triangles, equal angles guarantee proportional sides and proportional sides guarantee equal angles.
SSA is NOT a similarity criterion. Always write the vertices in the matching order.

example.q: A girl 1.5 m tall casts a 2 m shadow. At the same time a pole casts a 12 m shadow. How tall is the pole?
steps: The sun's rays make the same angle with the ground, and both stand at 90°, so the triangles are similar (AA)

learn.reallife: Surveyors find the height of a temple tower or a tall tree using a stick and shadows — no climbing needed!

games.title: Name the criterion
pairs: All three sides in the same ratio
One equal angle with the sides around it in the same ratio
A line parallel to one side of a triangle

games.title: Similar or not?
items: If two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the triangles are similar.
The third angles must also match, since each triangle's angles add to 180°.
SSA is a similarity criterion.
Two sides and a non-included angle do not fix the shape.
Triangles with sides 3, 4, 5 and 6, 8, 10 are similar.
Each ratio is 2, so they are similar by SSS.
Triangles with sides 2, 3, 4 and 4, 6, 9 are similar.
If ΔABC ~ ΔDEF, then AB/DE = BC/EF = CA/FD.
Corresponding sides follow the order of the letters.
Two triangles with one pair of equal angles are always similar.
One equal angle is not enough; you need two.

quiz.q: Two triangles have sides 4, 6, 8 cm and 6, 9, 12 cm. Are they similar, and by which criterion?
quiz.explain: 6/4 = 9/6 = 12/8 = 1.5. All three sides are in the same ratio, so the triangles are similar by SSS.
quiz.mistake: Thinks sides must be equal, not just proportional

quiz.q: Meena, 1.5 m tall, casts a 2.5 m shadow. At the same time a tower casts a 40 m shadow. How tall is the tower?
quiz.explain: The triangles are similar (AA), so height/shadow is equal: 1.5/2.5 = h/40, giving h = 24 m.
quiz.mistake: Uses shadow/height on one side and height/shadow on the other

quiz.q: In ΔABC and ΔPQR, ∠A = ∠P = 40° and AB/PQ = AC/PR = 2/3. By which criterion are they similar?
quiz.explain: An equal angle (∠A = ∠P) with the sides including it in the same ratio is the SAS criterion.
quiz.mistake: Calls it SSS without having the third pair of sides

quiz.q: In ΔABC, ∠A = 65° and ∠B = 45°. In ΔDEF, ∠D = 65° and ∠F = 70°. Are the two triangles similar, and with which vertex order?
options: Only if the sides are equal
quiz.mistake: Writes the vertices in the wrong matching order

quiz.q: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, with AB = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm, CA = 5 cm and PQ = 6 cm. What is the perimeter of ΔPQR?
quiz.explain: The scale factor is 6/3 = 2, so the perimeter is 2 × (3 + 4 + 5) = 24 cm.
quiz.mistake: Gives the perimeter of ΔABC

quiz.q: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 2 cm, AB = 6 cm and DE = 3 cm. What is BC?
quiz.explain: ΔADE ~ ΔABC by AA (corresponding angles are equal). So DE/BC = AD/AB = 2/6, giving BC = 3 × 6 ÷ 2 = 9 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses AD/DB = 2/4 instead of AD/AB

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a criterion for similarity of triangles?
quiz.explain: Two sides and an angle that is not between them do not fix the shape of a triangle.
quiz.mistake: Assumes any three parts are enough

quiz.q: In right ΔABC with ∠B = 90°, BD is drawn perpendicular to AC. Which triangle is ΔADB similar to?
quiz.explain: In ΔADB and ΔABC, ∠A is common and ∠ADB = ∠ABC = 90°. By AA, A ↔ A, D ↔ B, B ↔ C, so ΔADB ~ ΔABC.
quiz.mistake: Gets the order of the matching vertices wrong

teach.ask: Gappu has two triangles: 'Do I have to measure everything to know they are similar?'
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! AA, SSS or SAS — any one of these clues is enough. Detective Gappu is ready!
teach.nudge: What are the three shortcuts, and do sides need to be equal or just in the same ratio?

learn.hook: Once two triangles are similar, a whole treasure of equal ratios, products and angles opens up!
points: In the current book, the AA, SSS and SAS criteria are stated and used without proof — your job is to pick the right criterion and match the vertices correctly.
From similar triangles, write equal ratios and cross-multiply: if ΔPAC ~ ΔPDB then PA/PD = PC/PB, so PA × PB = PC × PD.
In similar triangles, corresponding medians and altitudes are in the same ratio as corresponding sides.
When two lines cross at O and AC ∥ BD, ΔOAC ~ ΔOBD (vertically opposite angles and alternate angles are equal).
In a right triangle ABC (∠C = 90°) with CD ⊥ AB: ΔACD ~ ΔABC, so AC² = AB × AD.

example.q: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR with AB = 6 cm and PQ = 9 cm. The median AD of ΔABC is 4 cm. Find the median PM of ΔPQR.
steps: Corresponding medians are in the ratio of the sides

learn.reallife: Architects use these ratios to scale every part of a building plan — not just the outer walls but every beam and diagonal.

games.title: Match the similarity to the result
pairs: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR with medians AD, PM

games.title: True or false?
items: In the current book, the SSS and SAS criteria are used without proof.
They are stated as results to apply.
Corresponding altitudes of similar triangles are in the ratio of their sides.
This follows from AA similarity of the smaller right triangles.
If two lines cross at O and AC ∥ BD, then ΔOAC ~ ΔOBD.
Vertically opposite angles at O and alternate angles give AA.
Ratios from similar triangles can be written in any vertex order.
The order must follow the correspondence of vertices.
If PA/PD = PC/PB, then PA × PD = PC × PB.
Cross-multiplying gives PA × PB = PC × PD.

quiz.q: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR with AB = 6 cm and PQ = 9 cm. The median AD is 4 cm. What is the corresponding median PM?
quiz.explain: Medians are in the ratio of the sides: PM = 4 × 9/6 = 6 cm.
quiz.mistake: Turns the ratio upside down

quiz.q: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF with BC = 8 cm and EF = 12 cm. The altitude from A is 6 cm. What is the altitude from D?
quiz.explain: Altitudes are in the ratio of the sides: 6 × 12/8 = 9 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds the difference of sides instead of using the ratio

quiz.q: In trapezium ABCD with AB ∥ DC, the diagonals meet at O. OA = 6 cm, OC = 4 cm and OB = 9 cm. What is OD?
quiz.explain: ΔOAB ~ ΔOCD (AA), so OA/OC = OB/OD. 6/4 = 9/OD gives OD = 6 cm.
quiz.mistake: Matches OB with OC instead of OD

quiz.q: Lines AB and CD cross at O with AC ∥ BD. OA = 4 cm, OB = 6 cm and AC = 5 cm. What is BD?
quiz.explain: ΔOAC ~ ΔOBD (vertically opposite and alternate angles). So BD/AC = OB/OA → BD = 5 × 6/4 = 7.5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the ratio upside down

quiz.q: From ΔPAC ~ ΔPDB, we get PA/PD = PC/PB. Which result follows?
quiz.explain: Cross-multiplying PA/PD = PC/PB gives PA × PB = PC × PD.
quiz.mistake: Cross-multiplies the wrong pairs

quiz.q: You are told the SAS similarity criterion without proof. What must you still check before using it?
options: That one angle is equal and the sides including it are in the same ratio
Nothing — any two triangles are similar
quiz.explain: SAS needs one pair of equal angles with the two sides making that angle in the same ratio.
quiz.mistake: Uses SAS with an angle that is not between the two sides

quiz.q: ΔODC ~ ΔOBA, where B, O, D lie on one straight line. If ∠BOC = 130°, what is ∠DOC?
quiz.explain: ∠BOC and ∠DOC form a linear pair on line BD, so ∠DOC = 180° − 130° = 50°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the two angles are equal instead of adding to 180°

quiz.q: In the same figure (ΔODC ~ ΔOBA, ∠DOC = 50°), ∠CDO = 65°. What is ∠OAB?
quiz.mistake: Matches the vertices in the wrong order

quiz.q: In right ΔABC with ∠C = 90°, CD ⊥ AB. If AB = 9 cm and AD = 4 cm, what is AC?
quiz.explain: ΔACD ~ ΔABC gives AC/AB = AD/AC, so AC² = AB × AD = 36 and AC = 6 cm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to take the square root

teach.ask: Gappu knows ΔPAC ~ ΔPDB but doesn't know what to do next. Show him how to get a useful result.
teach.praise: Tweet! Write the matching ratios in the right order, cross-multiply — and out pops PA × PB = PC × PD!
teach.nudge: Which sides go together in the ratios?

learn.hook: Walk away from a street lamp at night and your shadow stretches longer and longer. Similar triangles tell you exactly how long!
points: Lamp-post problems: the lamp-post and the person are both vertical, and the light ray makes the same angle with the ground. So the two triangles are similar (AA).
If the lamp is H high, the person h high, the person stands d from the post and the shadow is s long, then h/H = s/(s + d).
The farther the person walks, the longer the shadow.
Recap: similar figures; BPT and its converse; AA (AAA), SSS and SAS criteria for similar triangles.

example.q: A street lamp is 4.5 m high. A boy 1.5 m tall stands 6 m from its foot. How long is his shadow?
steps: Let the shadow be s m. Big triangle: height 4.5, base s + 6. Small triangle: height 1.5, base s

learn.reallife: Photographers and stage-lighting crews use this idea to predict how long a shadow will fall on the floor.

games.title: Solving a lamp-post problem
items: Draw the lamp-post, the person and the light ray
Spot two similar right triangles (AA)
Let the shadow be s and write h/H = s/(s + d)
Cross-multiply and solve for s
Check the answer is sensible (positive, not too long)

games.title: Recap: match the result
pairs: Line ∥ one side cuts the other two in the same ratio
Line cutting two sides in the same ratio is ∥ third side
One equal angle and including sides proportional

quiz.q: A street lamp is 4.5 m high. A boy 1.5 m tall stands 6 m from its foot. How long is his shadow?
quiz.mistake: Uses s/6 instead of s/(s + 6)

quiz.q: A lamp is 5 m high. Pooja, 1.25 m tall, walks away from it at 1 m/s. How long is her shadow after 6 seconds?
quiz.explain: After 6 s she is 6 m away. 1.25/5 = s/(s + 6) → 4s = s + 6 → s = 2 m.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the distance walked to the shadow for the big triangle

quiz.q: As a girl walks away from a lamp-post, what happens to the length of her shadow?
quiz.explain: s = hd/(H − h) grows as the distance d grows, so the shadow gets longer.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shadow behaves like a sunlight shadow, which does not depend on distance

quiz.q: At the same moment, a 2 m stick casts a 1.6 m shadow and a tower casts a 24 m shadow. How tall is the tower?
quiz.explain: Height/shadow is the same: h/24 = 2/1.6, so h = 24 × 2/1.6 = 30 m.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 1.6/2 instead of 2/1.6

quiz.q: Recap: in ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD/DB = 3/5 and AE = 6 cm. What is EC?
quiz.explain: By BPT, AE/EC = AD/DB = 3/5, so EC = 6 × 5/3 = 10 cm.
quiz.mistake: Turns the ratio the wrong way

quiz.q: Recap: two triangles have two pairs of equal angles. Which criterion says they are similar?
quiz.explain: Two equal angles force the third to be equal too, so AA (or AAA) applies.
quiz.mistake: Confuses similarity criteria with congruence criteria like RHS

quiz.q: Recap: are triangles with sides 5, 12, 13 cm and 10, 24, 26 cm similar?
options: Yes, by SSS, since every ratio is 1/2
No, only equilateral triangles can be similar
quiz.explain: 5/10 = 12/24 = 13/26 = 1/2, so the sides are proportional and SSS applies.
quiz.mistake: Thinks similar triangles must have equal sides

quiz.q: Recap: in ΔPQR, points S on PQ and T on PR satisfy PS/SQ = PT/TR. What can you conclude?
quiz.explain: By the converse of BPT, a line dividing two sides in the same ratio is parallel to the third side.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up BPT with its converse or with congruence

teach.ask: Gappu stands under a street lamp at night and wonders how long his shadow is. Explain how similar triangles help.
teach.praise: Chirp! The lamp-post and I make similar triangles, so h/H = s/(s + d). I can find my shadow!
teach.nudge: Which two triangles are similar, and what is the base of the big one?
